notes: SHIP v1.14.411 - THE LOADOUT PICKER, AND A REGRESSION v1.14.410 PUT ON PRODUCTION. THE REGRESSION FIRST, BECAUSE IT WAS MINE. v1.14.410 moved the grid and search utilities out of the rack row into a cluster hanging from the sheet header. In their new home they painted OVER the open loadout picker and document.elementFromPoint returned the cluster, not the picker - so a tap in that corner while choosing racks fired the loadout button instead of ticking a rack. Choosing racks is exactly when that picker is open, so this was reachable in ordinary use, not a corner case. THE CAUSE IS A STACKING CONTEXT, NOT A Z-INDEX TYPO. #forge3d-hud is position:absolute with z-index:5, which ESTABLISHES A STACKING CONTEXT, so every z-index declared inside it - the picker's 55, the search overlay's 50, the detail panel's 40 - is flattened to 5 when it competes at sheet level. The cluster lives OUTSIDE that context, because the header is position:relative with z-index:auto and therefore establishes none, so its own z-index competes with the HUD AS A WHOLE. At 6 it beat all three overlays. At 4 it sits above the static #forge3d-mount and below the entire HUD, which is exactly how .toprow behaved before the move. This is the v1.14.408 lesson running in the opposite direction: moving an element OUT of a stacking context silently changes what its z-index means, the same way that giving .hud position:fixed silently capped everything inside it. HOW IT WAS CAUGHT MATTERS. Rect measurement said the layout was perfect and it was - nothing moved a pixel, only the paint order changed. A SCREENSHOT of the open picker showed the two buttons floating on top of the modal. Geometry assertions cannot see paint order; the guard added below asserts hit-testing instead. THE PICKER ITSELF - and the single Orbitron line that started this was the smallest of five defects in it. (1) EVERY RACK ROW WAS 43px, one pixel under the 44px gloved floor, because .pick took its height from padding plus content instead of declaring it. That is the same shape as the .407 .hudbtn defect and it now takes min-height:var(--tap-s). (2) .pick .pid asked for 'Orbitron', for which this build ships no @font-face at all, so every rack ID in the picker silently rendered Helvetica; it takes --ff-display, which resolves, and --hud-track-data, because a rack ID is data. font-family:'Orbitron' is now at ZERO across the whole file. (3) .picker-rowhead was 9px, below the app's own declared 10px hard floor at :158. (4) THE COUNT WAS GOLD. '2/5' is a read-out, not a warning, and this is the third instance of the same misuse after API OFFLINE and the grid button the owner ruled on. Attention is the one channel that has to stay expensive, so a count that needs nobody does not get to spend it; it takes --ink and the cyan title stays the loud thing. (5) The checkbox radius was 4px, on no step of the R-B scale. GUARD: test/e2e/08-forge-layout.spec.js grows to 18 tests. The new one asserts the OUTCOME rather than the number, so any future z-index choice is free as long as it is correct: on the bare scene both utilities must be hit-testable (a control that renders but cannot be tapped is a dead control); with the picker open the PICKER must own those pixels; with the detail panel open neither button may; and after both close the buttons must come back, because a control permanently buried is the opposite failure. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4578/4578 balanced, CRLF intact with 0 lone LF, three-stamp lockstep. RACK SCENE LOCK respected - nothing under #forge3d-mount, forge3d_render, drawGuts or the camera rig. ?legacy=1 unaffected - every selector here is scoped to #forge3d-sheet, which is body.rd + .open gated. CONTEXT: the v1.14.410 phone regression suite finished green after that ship went out - 112 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed across 121 tests - so .410 is verified as shipped and this is a genuine follow-on, not a rollback. DEVICE-VERIFY, folded into the open batch pass: clear the service-worker cache, confirm v1.14.411, open the aisle, tap the grid button to open the loadout picker, and then TAP THE TOP-RIGHT CORNER WHERE THOSE BUTTONS WERE - the picker must receive it and the loadout button must not fire. Then confirm rack IDs in the picker are legible at arm's length, that every row is comfortable with a gloved finger, and that the count reads as information rather than as a warning.
